<explanation>
1. Identify the project type and purpose
   • Project type: A Python-based command-line scraping tool (CLI application)  
   • Purpose: Given an Instagram username or ID and a valid session ID, extract public profile information (emails, phone numbers, follower counts, bio, etc.)  

2. Analyze the file structure
   • setup.py – packaging script for PyPI/GitHub installation  
   • toutatis/ – root package  
     – __init__.py – initialization  
     – core.py – core logic and classes that perform HTTP requests, data parsing, and formatting  

3. Key insights from the README
   • The tool exposes two CLI commands (–u and –i) to trigger the same underlying logic  
   • Requires Python 3 and a valid session cookie from a logged-in Instagram session  
   • Outputs results to standard output in a formatted block  

4. Main components for the system diagram
   a. CLI Interface  
      – Argument parser (click, argparse, or custom)  
      – Commands “–u” and “–i” mapped to core functions  
   b. Core Engine (toutatis/core.py)  
      – Session Manager: accepts sessionID and attaches it to HTTP headers/cookies  
      – Request Layer: performs GET calls to Instagram endpoints (profile JSON or HTML)  
      – Data Parser: extracts fields (name, followers, email, phone, etc.) from response  
      – Formatter/Printer: formats the extracted fields into text output  
   c. External Service  
      – Instagram public API or web endpoints  
   d. Packaging & Deployment  
      – setup.py defines entry_point for CLI command “toutatis”  

5. Relationships and interactions
   • User invokes CLI → Argument Parser  
   • Parser calls Session Manager + Request Layer  
   • Request Layer interacts with Instagram over HTTPS  
   • Response flows into Data Parser → Formatter → STDOUT  

6. Architectural patterns and design principles
   • Separation of concerns – CLI parsing vs HTTP requests vs parsing vs formatting  
   • Single responsibility – each class or function in core.py handles one step  
   • Extensibility point – add new parsers or output formats without touching CLI logic  

7. Diagram-tailoring guidelines for this CLI scraping tool
   • Focus on core functionality and external integration  
   • Show the flow from user input through the tool to Instagram and back  
   • Highlight the extensibility point (e.g., if someone wanted to add JSON output or another target)  

8. Elements to include in the diagram
   • Clear component labels: “CLI Parser”, “Session Manager”, “Request Layer”, “Data Parser”, “Formatter”  
   • Directional arrows to show flow: Input → Parser → Session → Request → Parser → Output  
   • Color coding or shapes:  
     – Blue boxes for internal modules  
     – Green box for external service (Instagram)  
     – Grey cylinder or package icon for setup/packaging  
   • Annotations for protocols (HTTPS) and data formats (JSON/HTML/text)  

9. Final tips
   • Be very detailed and capture each core step in core.py  
   • Don’t overthink—break the tool into as many discrete components as you can  
   • Show how you could swap out the Data Parser or Formatter without changing the CLI  

Use this guidance to draft a system design diagram that faithfully represents Toutatis’s architecture, its interaction with Instagram, and its internal module boundaries.  
</explanation>
